Series::rad2deg¶

Back to Series API Reference

Signature¶

Series::rad2deg() const -> Series
Series& Series::rad2deg_()
Series& Series::rad2deg_() const

What It Does¶

rad2deg() converts an angle in radians to degrees, elementwise:

rad2deg(x) = x * 180 / pi

It is the inverse of deg2rad(), and the usual last step when a computation works in radians (as the inverse trig methods asin() / acos() / atan() and atan2() do) but the result should be reported in degrees.

pi/2 becomes 90, pi becomes 180.

An integer or boolean input is promoted to a floating-point result.

Parameters¶

None.

Returns¶

Series or Series& The angle in degrees. rad2deg_() overwrites the current storage.

Gradient¶

rad2deg() is differentiable. It is a scale by a constant:

d/dx rad2deg(x) = 180 / pi = 57.29578

In-Place Form¶

rad2deg_() is the in-place sibling of rad2deg(): it computes the same result and writes it back into self directly — mutating it (and any other handle sharing the same storage) instead of allocating a new Series — then returns a reference to self.

Despite being declared const at the call site — a quirk of how this method’s wrapper is generated, not a promise that self is left unchanged — rad2deg_() genuinely mutates the series it’s called on.

auto x = pluss::make_series({0.0, 1.5707963267948966, 3.141592653589793});
x.rad2deg_();
std::cout << x;

Output¶

pluss::Series(shape=[3], strides=[1], dtype=float64, platform=cpu, numel=3, contiguous=true)
data=[0, 90, 180]

Examples¶

Example 1. The common angles, in radians in and degrees out.

pluss::series::print(
    std::cout,
    pluss::make_series({0.0, 1.5707963267948966, 3.141592653589793}).rad2deg());

Output¶

Series(shape=[3], strides=[1], dtype=float64, platform=cpu, numel=3, contiguous=true)
data=[0.0000, 90.0000, 180.0000]

Example 2. An integer number of radians is promoted, not scaled by a truncated constant.

pluss::series::print(
    std::cout,
    pluss::make_series({57, 114}, pluss::ScalarType::Int64).rad2deg());

Output¶

Series(shape=[2], strides=[1], dtype=float64, platform=cpu, numel=2, contiguous=true)
data=[3265.8594, 6531.7189]

Each result is the exact x * 180 / pi.

Example 3. The gradient is the constant 180 / pi.

auto x = pluss::make_series({1.0, 2.0});
x.tracks_slope_(true);

x.rad2deg().sum().reverse();

std::cout << "dx=" << x.sensitivity();

Output¶

dx=pluss::Series(shape=[2], strides=[1], dtype=float64, platform=cpu, numel=2, contiguous=true)
data=[57.29578, 57.29578]

Example 4. Reporting an atan2() angle in degrees.

pluss::series::print(
    std::cout,
    pluss::make_series({1.0, 1.0}).atan2(pluss::make_series({1.0, -1.0})).rad2deg());

Output¶

Series(shape=[2], strides=[1], dtype=float64, platform=cpu, numel=2, contiguous=true)
data=[45.0000, 135.0000]

Gotchas And Failure Modes¶

  • The result is floating point even for an integer input.

  • NaN propagates.

  • rad2deg() and deg2rad() are exact inverses only up to floating-point rounding.

Summary¶

rad2deg(x) scales radians to degrees by 180 / pi:

  • inverse of deg2rad()

  • promotes integer and boolean input to floating point

  • differentiable, constant derivative 180 / pi
